title: A Veil for the Crown
premise: Noor Quintana has spent her life hiding the beast-speech that once got her mother burned, guiding smugglers through Thornfell's passes while keeping her heart as closed as her gift. When a dying courier presses a blood-marked map into her hands, she learns the Crown's heir sold his soul to the court beneath the mountain to end a war — and the court means to collect at the solstice. Hunted by royal wardens and the mountain's own hungry nobility, Noor gathers a found family of outcasts: a disgraced warden, a debt-ridden minstrel, and a crow who is more than a crow. To steal back a soul, she must offer the one thing she swore never to reveal — and in speaking truth to the deep court, she discovers love is not a betrayal of duty but its truest form. She returns the prince's soul at the cost of her own memories, only to find that family remembers for you.
about_author: Elodie Sterling is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction, and whose love of borderlands folklore seeps into every page. She writes from a stone cottage full of rescued animals who, she insists, talk back.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Toll
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She guides a smuggler caravan through a storm-wracked Thornfell pass, quietly bargaining with a rockslide-prone goat spirit to keep them alive. Establishes her hidden gift, her loneliness, and the fragile code that keeps her safe. Emotional beat: competence masking isolation.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Waystation
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A wounded courier staggers into a mountain waystation pursued by riders in royal grey. He recognizes something in her — perhaps the gift itself — and dies pressing a blood-marked map into her hands, whispering 'the solstice.' Emotional beat: dread arriving uninvited.

chapters.title: What the Crows Saw
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, with the crow Kess eavesdropping. Royal wardens sweep the valley hunting the map. Noor reads it by firelight: tunnels beneath Thornfell leading to a sealed court, marked with her mother's handwriting. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: The Warden Who Deserted
chapters.summary: Serevan's POV. A disgraced royal warden, Serevan Ashvale, catches Noor's trail but hesitates — he deserted after witnessing what the Crown did to soul-bargainers. He lets her go, then follows anyway. Emotional beat: duty curdling into doubt.

chapters.title: Debts in Duskmarket
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. In the smuggler town of Duskmarket she seeks passage and instead acquires companions: Tam, a minstrel gambling away a debt to the wrong people, and Kess, who speaks one human word too many. Emotional beat: reluctant beginnings of found family.

chapters.title: The Prince Without a Shadow
chapters.summary: Serevan's POV. Flashback interwoven with present pursuit: Prince Aldric ended the Border War by selling his soul to the court beneath the mountain; the realm prospers while he hollows. Serevan realizes Noor's map leads to the collection site. Emotional beat: horror dressed as statecraft.

chapters.title: Into the Weeping Stair
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The company descends through the Weeping Stair, a tunnel where water sings names of the dead. Noor's beast-speech grows louder underground — dangerous, intoxicating. First skirmish with warden outriders; Tam proves braver than his debts. Emotional beat: fear becoming trust.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. They glimpse the deep court: beautiful, insectile nobility who trade in memory and vow. Noor learns the map was drawn by her mother, who once bargained there — and lost. Emotional beat: inheritance as wound.

chapters.title: A Bargain Half-Remembered
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A memory-trader offers Noor her mother's final bargain in exchange for one of Noor's own memories. She pays, and learns her mother died trying to buy back a soul before her. Emotional beat: grief reframed as legacy.

chapters.title: Wardens at the Gate
chapters.summary: Serevan's POV. The warden company corners them; Serevan must choose between arrest and treason. He turns his blade on his former captain, buying the group escape but branding himself an outlaw. Emotional beat: the cost of conscience.

chapters.title: Kess Speaks
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Kess reveals herself: a court exile in crow-shape, sent long ago to watch the surface, now loyal to the strange warm creatures who fed her. She warns the solstice collection cannot be stopped from outside — someone must stand inside it. Emotional beat: loyalty beyond species.

chapters.title: The Hollow Prince
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. The prince, nearly empty, wanders his own palace unrecognized, writing letters to no one. He senses the map moving toward the mountain and feels, for the first time in years, something like hope. Emotional beat: longing without language.

chapters.title: What Duty Costs
chapters.summary: Noor and Serevan clash. He argues returning the soul restores the realm; she argues the realm was built on a child's ransom — Aldric was fifteen when the bargain was struck. Their fight cracks open into honesty about their own sacrifices. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in argument.

chapters.title: The Minstrel's Price
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam's creditors sell word of their route to the deep court. Guilt-ridden, he trades his most precious possession — his composed songs, held in a memory-vial — to buy the group a night's concealment. Emotional beat: art as sacrifice.

chapters.title: Doors of Bone and Salt
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The company breaches the inner court using her mother's cipher. Beast-speech floods Noor: every chained creature of the deep court cries out to her, and she answers, waking things better left sleeping. Emotional beat: power as responsibility.

chapters.title: The Collection
chapters.summary: Climax begins. At the solstice rite, the court prepares to consume Aldric's soul before the assembled Crown envoys. Noor walks into the rite openly, gift blazing, and demands audience — scandalizing both courts. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into defiance.

chapters.title: Speak, Beast-Speaker
chapters.summary: Climax. Noor challenges the court's claim: the bargain was made by a frightened boy, not a sovereign will, and is therefore void. The court counters by offering her everything she wants — her mother returned — if she abandons the prince. Emotional beat: temptation sharpened to a knife's edge.

chapters.title: The Weight of a Soul
chapters.summary: Climax continues. Noor refuses, offering instead her own memories of everyone she loves as surety. Serevan, Tam, and Kess each step forward to share the price, proving found family can hold what one person cannot. The court, bound by its own laws, must accept a shared bond. Emotional beat: love as legal force.

chapters.title: Solstice Breaking
chapters.summary: Climax resolves. The rite shatters; Aldric's soul tears free and returns to him mid-ceremony before the horrified Crown. The deep court retreats beneath the mountain, its claim broken, leaving Thornfell trembling. Noor wakes remembering nothing of the people around her. Emotional beat: victory shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: Strangers Who Stay
chapters.summary: Falling action, rotating POVs. Noor, memoryless, is cared for by three strangers who refuse to leave. Serevan tells her their story; Tam plays songs she doesn't recall writing for him; Kess refuses to be a stranger at all. Emotional beat: tenderness without obligation.

chapters.title: What Memory Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Fragments return — not through her own mind, but through the beasts and crows who remember her voice, and through her mother's recovered bargain, which the court released as part of the voided claim. She chooses to rebuild rather than mourn. Emotional beat: identity as choice, not archive.

chapters.title: A Veil Lifted
chapters.summary: Resolution. Months later, Noor guides travelers openly, gift unhidden, under a new accord between mountain and crown brokered by a restored Prince Aldric. Her found family gathers at the waystation where it began. She does not remember falling in love with Serevan — so she falls again, willingly. Emotional beat: home as something built together.
